reviewed_by: Claude review of autonomous browser commands
reason: BrowserAutomationBroker's fallback for the browser.* and proxy.replay tools validated the flat tool arguments ({tab_id, url, page_url, ...}, already schema-checked with additionalProperties false and no kind) against BrowserCommandCreateRequest, whose kind field is required, so pydantic rejected every call before enqueue_command ran: an autonomous browser mission could never navigate, observe, control, interact, extract, replay or capture evidence; only the research and proxy-config tools worked. The broker now builds the request with the tool name as kind, tab_id and page_url lifted out, and the remaining arguments nested. Separately, BrowserAutomationService.enqueue_command checked only expected_page_url when it was present, so a command whose arguments.url pointed outside the lease's target subset (or the engagement scope) was queued and dispatched as long as expected_page_url was in scope; both targets are now checked. test_browser_automation gains a broker call for browser.navigate that asserts the queued command's kind, tab, arguments and expected page (ValidationError on main) and an enqueue with an in-scope expected_page_url and an out-of-lease url that must be refused (queued on main); the file's other cases cover leases, claims, results, scope expansion and the research tools.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:browser-complete and area:core-api do not run an autonomous browser mission through the broker; the Python tests drive the broker and service directly. No full suites.
